title: OSHA Local Exhaust Ventilation Checklist (29 CFR 1910.94)
subtitle: For site inspections of abrasive blasting, grinding, polishing, buffing and spray finishing areas.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A; use N/A only for operations the area does not run.
For each Defect, record what was found, arrange the repair and recheck the item before the operation resumes.
The manufacturer's instructions and site rules may add checks; this list does not replace the full text of 29 CFR 1910.94.

sections.title: Abrasive blasting enclosures and exhaust
items: During blasting, air is drawn inward at every enclosure opening
Openings are baffled or arranged; no visible spurts of dust escape to adjacent areas
Multiple sets of slit abrasive-resistant baffles at small access openings, intact and not worn through
Doors are flanged and close tightly
Doors open from both inside and outside, or a small operator door is present where the large work door opens from outside only
Where hard deep-cutting abrasives are used, windows are safety glass protected by screening
No dust leaks on enclosure or ducts; any leak found earlier has been repaired
Pressure drop at exhaust ducts has been checked and shows no appreciable change pointing to a partial blockage
Where abrasive is recirculated, a separator removes fines from spent abrasive
Exhaust air passes through dust collecting equipment that can be emptied without contaminating other work areas

sections.title: Abrasive blasting PPE and housekeeping
items: Respirators in use carry NIOSH approval under 42 CFR part 84
Operators inside blast-cleaning rooms wear abrasive-blasting respirators covering head, neck and shoulders
A program under 29 CFR 1910.134 covers every employee using a respirator this section requires
Breathing air for blasting respirators meets 29 CFR 1910.134(i) and is free of harmful dusts, mists or gases
Operators wear heavy canvas or leather gloves and aprons, or equivalent
Provided to operators whose respirator lacks it and to others working nearby
Blast nozzle is bonded and grounded
No dust accumulation outside the enclosure; spills cleaned up
No steel shot or similar abrasive on walking surfaces

sections.title: Grinding, polishing and buffing hoods
items: Dust and dirt fall or are thrown into the hood in the direction of airflow
Wheels, discs, straps and belts do not throw dust toward the operator's breathing zone
Measured exhaust meets the Table G-4 minimum for the wheel diameter and width
Tongue works and sits within one-fourth inch of the wheel periphery
Where work permits, partial enclosure with minimal opening and average face velocity of at least 200 feet per minute
Operator stands outside the working face; average inward velocity at least 150 feet per minute
Exhaust system has a suitable dust collector in service

sections.title: Spray booths and spray rooms
items: Every spray-finishing job runs in a booth or dedicated spray room
Clear path at least 6 1/2 feet high from every work location to an exit or open front
Filters are in place and easy to reach for inspection, cleaning or replacement
Velocity into openings meets Table G-10 for the operating condition and booth size, unless an adequate air replacement system is fitted
Doors are closed while spray painting
Self-closing doors, dampers or louvers are fully open whenever spraying
Gage across filters is installed and marked with the cleaning or replacement pressure drop
Gage reading is below the marked change point and face airflow is not below Table G-10
No make-up air heating equipment inside the booth

references: 29 CFR 1910.94: Ventilation (Part 1910 Subpart G, Occupational Health and Environmental Control)
Source: eCFR, Title 29, text as of 2026-11-09
disclaimer: General guidance only, not legal advice. Check the current regulation and your employer's procedures.
